instruction_text: Warm, bright, cozy storytelling in the manner of a well-loved radio feature: unhurried, richly expressive, with full vowels and gentle emphasis, never flat or sleepy. Let the pitch rise and fall a little more on key words. Add a touch more brightness and a hint of a smile in the voice, while staying unhurried. Articulate crisply: distinct consonants, clean word endings, every syllable clearly heard.
asr_text: After that, an index showing world market prices fell by 25% in seven months. The USDA says this happened because more supplies became easier to get. But in the U.S., the coffee part of the Consumer Price Index was still higher. It was higher than in the same month a year earlier. Wait a minute, that doesn't add up. You might want to say that, but one is a world market index, and the other is the U.S. consumer price index. One shows a drop over seven months, while the other compares prices with a year earlier. They are on different stages and run on different clocks. If you pour the numbers into the same cup, the story gets muddled. And price tags follow their own schedule. Reuters spoke with market experts and others. They estimated that it takes around nine months or longer. That is how long green bean prices take to show up in store prices. If market prices are a breaking news alert, price tags are patient letters.
